question: Should upgrades intentionally change shared-profile browser behavior from three concurrent tabs with a bounded wait to one active tab with an unlimited queue wait by default?
rationale: The fairness bug can be fixed independently, but the proposed defaults alter established throughput and process-lifetime behavior, so source inspection cannot determine the intended product policy.

options.title: Preserve compatibility defaults
options.body: Land FIFO ordering and separate queue accounting while retaining three tabs and a finite derived queue timeout unless users explicitly configure serialization or unlimited waiting.

options.title: Adopt serialized unlimited waiting
options.body: Approve one active tab and an unlimited queue as the new defaults after the PR supplies live upgrade and stalled-holder proof.

options.title: Split fairness from defaults
options.body: Merge the queue correctness and session fixes first, then handle concurrency and timeout defaults in a separately reviewed change.

recommendation.title: Preserve compatibility defaults
recommendation.body: Land FIFO ordering and separate queue accounting while retaining three tabs and a finite derived queue timeout unless users explicitly configure serialization or unlimited waiting.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced and merged the current queue behavior and are best positioned to decide the repository's shared-profile default policy.
